resources.string: Choose light, dark, or follow your phone\'s system setting.
Periodic ping to the server while the tunnel is active; results are logged in Connection Log
Keep-alive target (host/URL only, no port -- automatically HTTP port 80)
TCP Connect: opens/closes a lightweight SOCKS5 handshake. HTTP Request: actually sends an HTTP request & waits for the server\'s reply (stronger proof the connection works).
Interval must be a number %1$d-%2$d seconds
Enter host only (port defaults to 443), or host:port (e.g. www.google.com:443)
Record high-detail errors (full stack traces, including crashes) to a local file on this device. Off by default -- turn it on only when you need to troubleshoot.

Once enabled, high-detail errors & warnings (including stack trace messages) will be recorded to a file on this device, AND shown live in the Log card on the Dashboard. The log may contain technical connection details. Only turn it on while troubleshooting, then turn it back off when done.

When turned on, the default DNS below is applied when the SSH/Xray profile\'s DNS 1/DNS 2 (set on the Configuration screen) are both empty. There is no built-in default -- enter the address yourself in the field below.
Off by default. Turn on if you want a default DNS applied when the profile DNS is empty.
Must be an IP address (e.g. 1.1.1.1), not a domain

Leave the ports below blank to use each profile\'s default. SOCKS5 Port overrides the port for every profile. HTTP Port turns on an additional local HTTP proxy (chained to SOCKS5) for apps that only support an HTTP proxy. UDPGW Port, if filled in, forwards non-DNS UDP (games, QUIC/HTTP3, VoIP) through a badvpn-udpgw process on the server (the server MUST already be running badvpn-udpgw on this port).
Prevent the CPU from sleeping while the tunnel is active, so the connection doesn\'t drop in the background
Automatically reconnect if the tunnel drops on its own (max. 3 attempts)
Turn on for full-traffic mode (downloads, speed tests, etc). When off, multitasking mode is used instead.
Compress SSH traffic with zlib -- reduces data usage at a small CPU cost.
Not applicable on this Android version
Not restricted -- the tunnel can safely run in the background
Optimized by the system -- the tunnel may disconnect in the background
The battery permission dialog isn\'t available on this device -- look for the battery menu manually on this page, or in the phone\'s built-in Security app
Couldn\'t open battery settings on this device
%1$s must be a number %2$d-%3$d, or leave it blank

Combine multiple connections into one (faster on high-RTT networks). Turn off if your Xray/VLESS account fails to connect or "connects but no traffic flows" -- some bug-host/CDN providers aren\'t compatible with Mux.
